name: IL-08
label: Likely D

key_factors: District leans D+5 and the national environment favors Democrats this cycle
Bean holds a roughly $5.5M outside-spending advantage with minimal Republican outside opposition
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot and no public general-election polling
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold near 95%
model.rationale: The district's five-point Democratic lean combined with a favorable environment points to a comfortable hold, and Bean's multi-million-dollar outside-spending edge reinforces it. With the incumbent off the ballot and no polling available, markets pricing the race near 95 percent Democratic argue for likely rather than safe.
model.watch: A late shift in the national environment or new polling showing Davis competitive would move this race toward tossup territory.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Raja Krishnamoorthi (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats defend an open suburban seat that leans five points their way, with Raja Krishnamoorthi leaving the House to run for Senate. Melissa Bean faces Republican Jennifer Davis, who has raised substantial money of her own but lacks comparable outside backing. Allied groups have poured millions into boosting Bean, while Republican-side outside spending has been minimal.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and a national environment that favors Democrats this cycle. Prediction markets price a Democratic hold at roughly 95 percent. The seat is expected to stay Democratic, though the open-seat dynamic and absence of polling leave somewhat more uncertainty than in a typical held district.
